stem.text: A $100\,\text{cm}$ potentiometer wire QT is connected in series with a $2.00\,\text{V}$ cell. Another circuit, consisting of a $2.00\,\text{V}$ cell in series with resistors of resistance $4.00\,\Omega$ and $6.00\,\Omega$, is set up alongside the potentiometer. Connections PQ and RS are then made so that the potential difference (p.d.) across the $4.00\,\Omega$ resistor is balanced against the p.d. across a length $L$ of potentiometer wire. Both cells have negligible internal resistance.

stem.alt: Circuit diagram with a potentiometer wire from Q to T along the top, a 2.00 V cell above it, a second 2.00 V cell below, resistors labelled 4.00 Ω and 6.00 Ω, a sliding contact at S, a galvanometer, a point R, and a length L marked along the wire from Q to S.
